nodes.description: Zdhhc9 knockout mice have grossly normal oligodendrocyte development but extensive morphological and structural myelin abnormalities. In the corpus callosum the balance of mature oligodendrocyte subtypes shifts away from myelination-associated MOL2/3 cells, myelinated axon density falls, myelin compaction is disrupted, and genes and proteins for lipid metabolism and cholesterol synthesis are reduced.

evidence.reference_title: Epilepsy, cognitive deficits and neuroanatomy in males with ZDHHC9 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in ZDHHC9 are associated with susceptibility to focal seizures and specific cognitive impairments intersecting with the RE spectrum.

nodes.description: Global or segmental callosal hypoplasia was seen in seven of nine males on blinded MRI review, was present before seizure onset, and was stable over time. A dysplastic corpus callosum was reported in another family.

nodes.description: DHHC9 needs GCP16 for stability and acyltransferase activity; only the folded DHHC9-GCP16 complex is active. Disease alleles lower the autopalmitoylated enzyme intermediate and reduce complex formation, so less palmitate is transferred to substrate proteins.

evidence.reference_title: DHHC9 and GCP16 constitute a human protein fatty acyltransferase with specificity for H- and N-Ras.
evidence.snippet: DHHC9 and GCP16 form a protein complex, and DHHC9 requires GCP16 for protein fatty acyltransferase activity and protein stability

evidence.reference_title: GCP16 stabilizes the DHHC9 subfamily of protein acyltransferases through a conserved C-terminal cysteine motif.
evidence.snippet: only properly folded DHHC9-GCP16 complex is enzymatically active in vitro

evidence.reference_title: Regulation of RAS palmitoyltransferases by accessory proteins and palmitoylation.
evidence.snippet: demonstrating that GCP16 and Erf4 are not directly involved in the catalytic process but stabilize the architecture of DHHC9 and Erf2, respectively

nodes.description: Zdhhc9 knockout mice show seizure-like activity together with increased frequency and amplitude of spontaneous and miniature excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic currents. That the synapse-level change causes the network-level hyperexcitability is the authors' interpretation, not a demonstrated step.

nodes.description: ZDHHC9 is the most highly expressed protein acyltransferase in myelinating oligodendrocytes and localizes to Golgi outposts in their processes, whereas XLID mutant forms stay in the cell body. ZDHHC9 palmitoylates myelin basic protein, and MBP palmitoylation is reduced in knockout brain.

evidence.reference_title: Micro-scale control of oligodendrocyte morphology and myelination by the intellectual disability-linked protein acyltransferase ZDHHC9.
evidence.snippet: we found that ZDHHC9 palmitoylates Myelin Basic Protein (MBP) in heterologous cells, and that palmitoylation of MBP is impaired in the Zdhhc9 knockout brain

evidence.reference_title: Micro-scale control of oligodendrocyte morphology and myelination by the intellectual disability-linked protein acyltransferase ZDHHC9.
evidence.snippet: Wild-type ZDHHC9 localizes to Golgi outposts in OL processes, but other PATs and XLID mutant forms of ZDHHC9 are restricted to OL cell bodies.

nodes.description: DHHC9-GCP16 palmitoylates H-Ras and N-Ras, which sets their distribution between Golgi and plasma membrane. In cultured hippocampal neurons Zdhhc9 acts through Ras to promote dendrite growth. Whether Ras palmitoylation is reduced in the intact brain is uncertain: it was not disrupted in Zdhhc9 mutant mouse brain.

animal_models.description: H-Ras palmitoylation was preserved in mutant brain.

evidence.reference_title: DHHC9 and GCP16 constitute a human protein fatty acyltransferase with specificity for H- and N-Ras.
evidence.snippet: Here we report that H- and N-Ras are palmitoylated by a human protein palmitoyltransferase encoded by the ZDHHC9 and GCP16 genes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ZDHHC9, which encodes a palmitoyltransferase of NRAS and HRAS, cause X-linked mental retardation associated with a Marfanoid habitus.
evidence.snippet: The degree of palmitoylation determines the temporal and spatial location of these proteins in the plasma membrane and Golgi complex.

evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, membrane association and S-acylation of H-Ras was not disrupted in either whole brain or hippocampus of Zdhhc9 mutant mice, suggesting that other substrates of this enzyme are linked to the observed changes.

nodes.description: Zdhhc9 palmitoylates the small GTPase TC10 (RHOQ) in neurons, and this is the route by which it promotes inhibitory synapse formation in hippocampal cultures.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ZDHHC9, which encodes a palmitoyltransferase of NRAS and HRAS, cause X-linked mental retardation associated with a Marfanoid habitus.
evidence.snippet: We have identified one frameshift mutation, one splice-site mutation, and two missense mutations in highly conserved residues in ZDHHC9 at Xq26.1 in 4 of 250 families with X-linked mental retardation (XLMR).

nodes.description: Hemizygous frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, intragenic deletion and missense variants in ZDHHC9. Missense and nonsense changes cluster at arginine residues in the cytoplasmic domains. All reported classes are consistent with loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: ZDHHC9 X-linked intellectual disability: Clinical and molecular characterization.
evidence.snippet: Missense, nonsense, frameshift, and splicing variants, in addition to large exonic deletions, have been described suggesting a loss of function mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: The X-Linked Intellectual Disability Gene Zdhhc9 Is Essential for Dendrite Outgrowth and Inhibitory Synapse Formation.
evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function mutations in ZDHHC9 have been identified in patients with X-linked intellectual disability (XLID) and associated with increased epilepsy risk.

nodes.description: Knockout mice show seizure-like activity and altered spontaneous and miniature postsynaptic currents.

Knockout corpus callosum shows shifted mature oligodendrocyte subtypes, fewer myelinated axons, disrupted myelin compaction and reduced lipid and cholesterol synthesis genes; sparse labeling shows myelin sheath abnormalities and loss of MBP palmitoylation.

Male Zdhhc9 mutant mice show reduced anxiety-like behaviour, reduced hang time suggesting hypotonia, spatial learning and memory deficits in the Morris water maze, and a 36% smaller corpus callosum on MRI.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of the Zdhhc9 intellectual disability gene leads to behavioural abnormalities in a mouse model.
evidence.snippet: deficits in the Morris water maze test of hippocampal-dependent spatial learning and memory
